mutants.description: The accumulator's capture gate is S_RUN only, while episode_start still uses convertor_running (S_SS or S_RUN), so the two blocks no longer agree during soft start
mutants.reason: A cause that is live during soft start (for example window_trip_SS or OTP while ss_active) is not recorded in fault_reg. Because fault_reg stays empty, episode_start fires on every clock, so fault_time keeps following timestamp_ms while fault_reg reads 0.

mutants.description: The episode-start detector uses the debounced SCR readback latch_state where the accumulator uses the CPLD's latch_assert, so a CPLD trip opens no episode until the readback follows
mutants.reason: When latch_assert is the first cause while running (for example right after a host read cleared the record), the accumulator sets the LATCH bit on that clock. latch_state is still low, so episode_start never fires and fault_time stays 0 while fault_reg is non-empty.

mutants.description: OVERCURRENT is recorded only when the window trip has already led to a CPLD latch trip, as if an overcurrent only counts once strikes reach the trip
mutants.reason: A window_trip or window_trip_SS that does not (yet) assert latch_assert, i.e. one strike below the limit, leaves bit 0 of fault_reg clear. The original records it on the first window trip.

mutants.description: LATCH_ASSERT is recorded only in S_RUN, on the assumption that the CPLD trips the latch only from run-time strikes, so a latch trip during soft start is forgotten
mutants.reason: If latch_assert rises while ss_active is high (an overcurrent in soft start), bit 3 of fault_reg is not set. The original records it whenever the converter is in S_SS or S_RUN.

mutants.description: A soft-start overcurrent window trip is filed under the LATCH_ASSERT (OCP/SCP) bit instead of the OVERCURRENT bit
mutants.reason: When window_trip_SS asserts during soft start with latch_assert low, fault_reg reads 01000 instead of 00001.

mutants.description: The OTP and UVLO cause bits are laid out in swapped positions, with the priority order between them misremembered
mutants.reason: An over-temperature while running sets fault_reg bit 1 instead of bit 2, and an undervoltage sets bit 2 instead of bit 1, so the host reads 00010 for OTP and 00100 for UVLO.
